_doc: One file per place. build.py renders /states/<slug>/ (kind=state) or /countries/<slug>/ (kind=country) from this file. Every number must be an official published figure with its source. Amounts in US dollars. Headline is Census state + local debt (same source and definition for every state); the state's own fresher, narrower figure is the secondary line.
name: Texas
cadence: Annual. The Census Bureau's Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances comes out about two years after the fiscal year (survey year 2024: July 2026; survey year 2023: July 2025).
next_update: The next Census figures, for survey year 2025, are expected around mid-2027, based on the last two release dates. The state's own report (shown as a secondary line) updates sooner.
fiscal_year_end_note: Texas's state fiscal year ends August 31, so Census survey year 2024 holds the state's fiscal year ended Aug 31, 2023; local governments' years vary. Census survey year 2024 covers each government's fiscal year that ended between July 1, 2023 and June 30, 2024; the clock dates it June 30, 2024, the end of that window.

legend: Texas state + local debt is reported once a year by the Census Bureau, about two years after the fact. Real borrowing happens in lumps when bonds are sold and is repaid on schedules, so the live number is a straight-line projection from the latest Census year, shown here next to the official totals.
notes: Census publishes Texas's state + local total as $389.33 billion for 2024 (coefficient of variation 0.89%) and $358.18 billion for 2023. State + local here is exactly Census's state figure plus its local figure.

Census's figures are the newest official state + local totals that use one definition for all 50 states, but they lag about two years, so the live clock projects from June 30, 2024. The state's own report (Texas Bond Review Board, FY2025) is fresher and counted differently; it is shown separately and never added. For the same year the two agree closely: the board's FY2023 state + local total is $380.65 billion, against Census's $389.33 billion for survey year 2024, which holds Texas's FY2023.

About the Bond Review Board figure: The local report's summary bullet says $368.30 billion ($256.64B tax-supported, $111.66B revenue), but its own Tables 1.1 and 1.3 and its Chapter 1 text say $368.89 billion ($257.02B and $111.86B). We use the table figure.
About the Bond Review Board figure: State and local totals come from separate Bond Review Board reports and are added as published; the board does not publish a combined total for the same date.
Not included: unfunded pension and retiree-health liabilities, and the state's share of the federal debt.
